top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY San Juan's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before race day.
GFNY San Juan's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.

Road-specific control matters at GFNY San Juan. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 95 miles.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
At mile 60 of 95, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY San Juan. Train it until it feels boring.
At GFNY San Juan, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at GFNY San Juan. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 95 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 4,265ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for GFNY San Juan’s 95 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at GFNY San Juan. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at GFNY San Juan rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, TT Threshold, and Road Specific to prepare you for 95 miles of mixed terrain in San Juan, Argentina.
